statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail 14% (low), Stress 49% (elevated), Confidence 86% (high), dominant mode mixed. The CME maintenance break runs 21:00Z to 22:00Z, so there is no live NQ tape. The futures day closed at 31,339.50, about 31 points under the 31,370.75 extreme, and cash closed 31,076.44, about 41 points under its 31,117.36 record high.
recommendation: Tail eases a further three points to 14%, deeper inside the low band, so the deterministic mapping returns EA_ON and green for both NQ futures and the NAS100 CFD. The futures day has now closed and the final tick of 31,339.50 at 20:59:58Z sits roughly 31 points beneath the 31,370.75 extreme, almost unchanged from 31,336.00 at 20:18:29Z an hour earlier. Price spent the whole closing stretch beneath a rejected high without reclaiming it, and the cash index closed 31,076.44, about 41 points under its own 31,117.36 record. VIX settled 15.52 near the bottom of a 15.48 to 16.38 range. A held retracement confirmed through the close is the opposite of the repeated-extension structure that would justify the block threshold. Tail does not fall further because the advance is unresolved rather than reversed, with the index within roughly 0.1% of an all-time high and the Globex reopen at 22:00Z still to test the 31,339.50 settlement. Tail remains well below the block threshold; the narrow evidence-based danger window stays at Fed Williams 13:05Z and the Oct 6 cash open at 13:30Z.
headline: Tail eases to 14% as the futures day closes 31 points under its 31,370.75 extreme; the CME break leaves no live tape until the 22:00Z reopen
body:
The single most important fact of this hour is structural rather than directional: the CME equity-index maintenance break runs from 21:00Z to 22:00Z, so there is no live NQ price path to assess. The futures day has closed and the next continuous evidence arrives with the Globex reopen at 22:00Z.

What the final 40 minutes of that futures day showed is the reason the published value eases again. The last NQZ26 tick was 31,339.50 at 20:59:58Z, up 277.75 points or 0.89% on the 31,061.75 prior close, against a 31,059.00 open and a day range of 30,957.50 to 31,370.75. An hour ago the verified quote was 31,336.00 at 20:18:29Z, roughly 35 points beneath the same extreme. Price therefore spent the entire closing stretch sitting about 31 to 35 points under the session high without reclaiming it. A flat drift beneath a rejected extreme is the opposite of the repeated-extension structure that denies a reverse or grid strategy its retracements.

The cash market closed in the same shape. NASDAQ-100 finished at 31,076.44, up 268.51 points or 0.87% on a 30,807.93 prior close, about 41 points under its 31,117.36 session high, having traded 30,798.42 to 31,117.36. That 31,117.36 print is also the 52-week high, so the index set a record and then declined to close beneath it. Tail falls from 17% to 14% because the held retracement is now confirmed through the close rather than observed mid-fade.

Volatility corroborates the orderly resolution. VIX settled at 15.52, up 0.21 points or 1.37% on a 15.31 prior close but near the bottom of a 15.48 to 16.38 range, having opened at 16.24. Implied volatility compressed through a record-setting session, which is not the signature of violent directional repricing.

Tail does not fall further than 14% because the advance itself is unresolved rather than reversed. The index closed within roughly 0.1% of an all-time high, and whether the Globex reopen accepts or rejects the 31,339.50 settlement is a genuine open question. That is why the modelled path holds a 10% overnight floor instead of returning to the 3% levels published late on Oct 4.

The amplifier stack stayed conflicting rather than aligned through Oct 5, and that remains the main cap on the published value. Breadth was the clearest constraint: advancing issues led decliners by only 1.04-to-1 on the NYSE and 1.09-to-1 on the Nasdaq beneath a record index level. The semiconductor complex split rather than confirmed. Taiwan Semiconductor gained about 2% to a record 484.19 dollars after Elon Musk confirmed early-stage talks about a role in his Texas Terafab venture, and Broadcom rose about 2%, yet Qualcomm fell about 2%, Intel dropped about 4%, and the Philadelphia chip index was about 0.3% lower. A record index level built on near one-to-one breadth with the chip group flat to lower is a megacap-led advance, not the broad alignment that produces an index-level one-way path.

Cross-assets conflict in the same direction. The 10-year Treasury yield closed at 5.31%, up about 3 basis points, inside a 5.26% to 5.35% range, with the 2-year reported around 4.844%; the Federal Reserve H.15 release shows 4.83% and 5.28% for the 2-year and 10-year as of Oct 2, and the 30-year at 5.63%. The long end therefore sits near its highest levels since 2002 while equities set records. Critically for Tail, the yield move was contained within a 9 basis point range rather than a disorderly spike, so this is a valuation conflict that belongs in Stress. Crude eased in the same risk-positive direction: WTI settled 89.30 dollars, down 1.81 dollars or 1.99%, inside an 88.74 to 91.88 range, with Brent near 101.59 dollars, as rising Middle East exports and a Group of Seven stock release offset Gulf supply concerns.

Composition reinforces the point. A material share of the Oct 5 move was idiosyncratic deal flow rather than index structure: PTC rose about 34.6% on Schneider Electric's 22.6 billion dollar acquisition, RXO gained about 22.5% on a 5.8 billion dollar C.H. Robinson agreement, and Cerebras Systems added about 9.5% after praise from OpenAI's chief executive. Single-stock merger and partnership moves do not create a one-way index path.

The macro backdrop is identifiable and unchanged from the prior hour. September ISM Services printed 54.9% at 14:00Z, a 0.5 point decrease from August's 55.4% and the 27th consecutive month of expansion, with Business Activity at 56.5%, New Orders at 59.8%, Employment back in expansion at 50.1% and Prices at 74.0%. Hot services prices alongside a soft September payroll print of 29,000 explain why the long end has stayed firm even as October rate-hike expectations receded. Stress eases two points to 49% and stays in the elevated band, because the valuation conflict and the unresolved Middle East supply picture both persist while realised volatility decays.

Confidence is 86%, one point below the prior hour. Complete verified settlement levels are in hand for NQ futures, the cash index, VIX, the 10-year yield and WTI, together with the ISM detail, breadth ratios and a verified seven-day calendar. The single deduction is that this specific clock-hour has no price path at all because of the scheduled exchange break, so current structure cannot be observed, only inferred from the close.

The narrow evidence-based danger window stays at 13:00Z to 15:00Z on Oct 6, covering Fed Williams at 13:05Z, the 13:30Z cash open and Fed Bowman at 14:45Z. An opening auction that continues from a record close with shallow pullbacks is the specific structure that would justify the watch band, and it is where the modelled path peaks at 17%. Every one of the 24 modelled slots stays inside the low band, and every forward value is conditional risk rather than an assertion that any future price path has been observed.

The shared Finviz context file was read and not used. Its generatedAt is 2026-09-29T23:14:22Z, roughly six days old, its collectionStatus is partial, and its futures section reports coverageStatus unavailable with all ten requested symbols missing. It falls far outside the 90-minute freshness bound and cannot support current cross-asset evidence. Every level cited above was fetched independently from primary and reputable current sources instead, which is why Confidence holds at 86% despite the unavailable shared feed.

lookbackSummary: Across the 24 hours to 20:00Z, Claude published Tail between 3% and 20% and Stress between 46% and 71%. Twenty-three of the 24 hours mapped to EA_ON and green; the single exception was 19:00Z, which reached 20% and was the only WATCH and yellow hour, as NQ pinned itself within about 9 points of a fourth record extreme into power hour. Tail sat at 3% through the Oct 4 US evening, rose into a 12% to 15% overnight band, troughed at 6% during the European morning, climbed in steps through the US session from 7% at midday to 17%, 18%, 19% and finally 20%, then eased back to 17% once the power-hour continuation failed to develop. Stress fell steadily from 71% late on Oct 4 to 46% by midday Oct 5 before firming to 54% as the long end pressed to multi-decade highs, closing the window at 51%. Dominant mode was normal overnight, briefly trend-down at 10:00Z, mixed through most of the US morning, and trend-up at 14:00Z and again from 17:00Z through the close. One hour, 06:00Z on Oct 5, has no published assessment and is marked unavailable rather than filled in.
outlookSummary: The modelled path treats the Oct 6 US cash open, not the Oct 5 futures close, as the next window where risk could approach the watch band. Tail opens at 14% for the 21:00Z hour, three points below the prior publication, because the fade off the 31,370.75 extreme held through the entire closing stretch and this clock-hour falls inside the 21:00Z to 22:00Z CME maintenance break with no live tape. It then eases through 12% and 11% as the Globex reopen is tested, reaching a 10% overnight floor across the Tokyo and Asian mid-session hours with Stress bottoming at 44%. That floor sits above the 3% levels published late on Oct 4 because the record cash close is unresolved overnight. Risk rebuilds through the European session, with mode shifting to mixed at the 07:00Z European open, then tracks the Oct 6 calendar: 14% across the 12:15Z weekly ADP and 12:30Z balance of trade block, a 17% peak spanning Fed Williams at 13:05Z, the 13:30Z cash open and Fed Bowman at 14:45Z, easing through 15% and 14% into the 17:00Z 3-year note auction, 13% afterwards, 14% into the Oct 6 power hour and 13% at the cash close. Every one of the 24 slots stays inside the low band and maps to EA_ON and green. Forward values are conditional risk, not an assertion that any future price path has been observed.
